items.title: When BFS finds the cheapest path
items.prompt: Breadth-first search is guaranteed to return a least-cost path when:

examEligibility.rationale: Practice-pool item: never exam-eligible by design; kept separate from the exam pool to protect exam integrity.

hints: Rule out each option that contradicts the definition, then check what is left.

feedback.correct: Correct. BFS finds the shallowest goal, which is the cheapest only when all steps cost the same. With varied costs, use uniform-cost search.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. BFS finds the shallowest goal, which is the cheapest only when all steps cost the same. With varied costs, use uniform-cost search.

criteria.description: Selects the option consistent with the definition.

privateAuthorNotes: Owner content review: check wording, correctness and distractor quality.

options.text: Every action has the same cost
Action costs are any positive numbers

answer.explanation: BFS finds the shallowest goal, which is the cheapest only when all steps cost the same. With varied costs, use uniform-cost search.

items.title: Why pick depth-first search
items.prompt: What is the main advantage of depth-first search over breadth-first search?

examEligibility.rationale: Practice-pool item: never exam-eligible by design; kept separate from the exam pool to protect exam integrity.

hints: Rule out each option that contradicts the definition, then check what is left.

feedback.correct: Correct. DFS keeps only the current path plus siblings, so memory grows with depth. It is neither optimal nor complete on infinite graphs.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. DFS keeps only the current path plus siblings, so memory grows with depth. It is neither optimal nor complete on infinite graphs.

criteria.description: Selects the option consistent with the definition.

privateAuthorNotes: Owner content review: check wording, correctness and distractor quality.

options.text: It needs much less memory, roughly proportional to depth
It always finds the shortest path
It is complete on infinite graphs

answer.explanation: DFS keeps only the current path plus siblings, so memory grows with depth. It is neither optimal nor complete on infinite graphs.
